calibration24h.interpretation: Higher confidence did correspond to better outcomes across every band (39% at 20-40 rising to 53% at 40-60). Observed rates differ from the score's implied probability by 6.0 points on average, so this is NOT a probability and must not be presented as one.

calibration7d.interpretation: Higher confidence did correspond to better outcomes across every band (50% at 20-40 rising to 53% at 40-60). Observed rates differ from the score's implied probability by 11.7 points on average, so this is NOT a probability and must not be presented as one. The spread between the least and most confident bands is under 5 points, which is small enough that confidence adds little discriminating power in practice.

walkForward.methodology: The execution engine has no fitted parameters: every threshold is a source-code constant and every percentile is ranked against prior history only. There is therefore nothing to train, and a conventional train/test split would be theatre — refitting nothing would reproduce identical decisions. These folds instead measure (a) whether the edge PERSISTS across sequential unseen periods, and (b) a genuine out-of-sample test: rank the two sides on discovery data alone, then check whether that ranking held in the following window. Discovery sets exclude any trade still open at the boundary (purge + embargo), so no validation-period price action can reach back into a discovery statistic.
walkForward.interpretation: Per-fold net expectancy ranged -0.651% to 1.614%, positive in 3 of 5 folds, averaging 0.681% against the pooled 0.386%. Sequential periods differ from the pooled figure by 0.295 points on average. The discovery-period side ranking held in 1 of 2 validation windows.

quantileCalibration.interpretation: Observed rates do NOT rise monotonically across quantiles, spanning -2.6 points from the lowest to the highest confidence quartile. The confidence intervals of the lowest and highest buckets overlap, so even the observed spread is not statistically distinguishable from no effect.

planner.timeStopFinding: NO TIME STOP is justified by this data: eventual win rate RISES with age, from 49.7% for trades open at hour 24 (n=1121) to 60.1% at hour 144 (n=767) — stops resolve faster than targets, so surviving trades are the good ones and a time stop would amputate winners. The hypothesized exit-if-below-45% trigger never fires at any measured horizon.
